newsitem.title: UK: British Post Office sticks stamp prices until 1998.
newsitem.headline: British Post Office sticks stamp prices until 1998.

text.p: Britain's state-owned Post Office stuck a 15-month price freeze on the cost of its stamps for ordinary first and second-class mail on Monday.
The Post Office said that the price limit was in spite of a series of strikes last year by postmen and sorting office staff.
Prices will remain at 26p for first class and 20p for second class stamps until at least April 1998, unchanged since a one penny increase in July last year.

"There will be no price increase at all in 1997. This means that our prices on first class postage are running at 14 percent below inflation (calculated) over the last 15 years," chief executive John Roberts said in a statement.
Last July's price rise itself followed a two-and-a-half year freeze, and the office said that it had only been broken by the pressure of a "steep hike in government cash demands".

"In the longer term, while it is clear that international prices will eventually have to rise because of higher charges imposed by other countries for delivering mail abroad, the Post Office will aim to maintain the pattern of reducing real prices within Britain," Roberts added.
This tactic would "undoubtedly boost home shopping and the expansion of communications generally", he said.
